source: Paul Silvia & Vi Bui, 'When Humor Lands or Flops: Data and Research Materials', OSF component https://osf.io/vnw2p of the project 'Psychology of Dad Jokes' (https://osf.io/bx9uz), created and posted 2026-10-06, licence CC BY-NC 4.0 (OSF API, license 60bf992258510b0009a5a9a6). Data and materials for their paper 'When Humor Lands or Flops: Exploring Positive and Negative Aspects of Dad Joke Experiences'; the paper itself was not found tonight.
committed: no raw file; only the 72 jokes used tonight with the derived per-joke funniness means and rater counts in people.json, with attribution, non-commercial

files.name: Joke_Aesthetics_Joke_Level_240_OSF.csv
files.what: One row per joke (240): its text, its survey position (serial_survey_id), the mean of its 1-5 funniness ratings (funny_joke_5mean) and the number of raters (funny_joke_completed)

files.name: Joke_Aesthetics_Person_Level_OSF.csv
files.what: One row per rater (541 Prolific adults): every joke rating; read to check that the joke-level means are the raters' means (240 of 240 agree, matched by survey position, not by joke_id)

files.name: When_Humor_Lands_Flops_Qualtrics_Codebook_OSF.docx
files.what: The survey as shown: the instruction ('dad jokes ... short, clean jokes that try to be funny by using puns and wordplay', 'there's no right or wrong answer') and the 1 (Not at all) to 5 (Extremely) scale for Funny
